free_tier.stated: StorageBox 16 TB - USA: 16 TB NVMe Cached HDD, 80 TB bandwidth @ 10 Gbps, $35.50 a month or $355.00 a year, hosted in Utah, USA.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The order page states no per-object size limit; the largest plan lists 16 TB of NVMe Cached HDD.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention period for stored files is stated. The terms page states unpaid services are terminated three days past the due date and active data and backups are destroyed.

egress.terms: Bandwidth is quoted as a hard multiple of storage. "5 TB Bandwidth @ 10 Gbps" on 1 TB, "40 TB" on 8 TB, "80 TB" on 16 TB. So 5x storage per month. NOT unmetered. A LET poster claims "its actually unmetered if you know how to set it up". Treat that as unverified forum folklore, not a policy.

interface_detail: SSH, FTP and rSync; DirectAdmin Control Panel
tooling: rsync/rclone-over-SFTP only. No S3, no WebDAV, no object API.
chaining: Protocol support is limited to SFTP, rsync, and Borg without native WebDAV or S3 interfaces. Well-suited for backend backup targets rather than public origin distribution.
limits_note: DirectAdmin is a web-hosting panel bolted onto storage. You manage FTP users and bandwidth there. RAID-6 (DE) / RAID-60 (500 GB) at order-page level. US inventory and DE inventory are separate products with separate coupons.
reliability_note: Real hosting business (labze), 2+ years on LET with a Patron Provider tag; users report multi-year renewals at the same price, which is rare. But it is a small operator reselling/colocating, not owning DCs. And the 500 GB SKU is excluded from BFBOX by design.

extras.chaining_verbatim: Weakest chaining of the top candidates: no WebDAV means AList mounting requires an SFTP shim, and no S3 means no presigned URLs. Fine as a pure rsync/Borg target behind an app server; poor as a served origin.
extras.tooling_verbatim: rsync/rclone-over-SFTP only. No S3, no WebDAV, no object API.
extras.interface_verbatim: SSH, FTP, rsync, SFTP, DirectAdmin panel. **No WebDAV, no SMB** — confirmed by LET users comparing it to Hetzner.
extras.price_verbatim: List: $1.85/TB/mo at 16 TB ($355/yr), $1.93 at 8 TB. With BFBOX 40% recurring on yearly: 16 TB = $213/yr = $1.11/TB/mo; 8 TB = $111/yr = $1.16/TB/mo; 4 TB = $57/yr = $1.19/TB/mo. 5 TB workload: 8 TB plan = $1.16/TB/mo. 20 TB workload: two 16 TB boxes = $2.22/TB/mo (16 TB is their ceiling, so the discount curve breaks at the 20 TB archive size). Caveat: no WebDAV/SMB and egress = 5x storage.
extras.agent_focus: The cheap-paid lane — where bulk storage is actually bought (LowEndTalk offers, LowEndBox, r/DataHoarder, Slickdeals, 什么值得买, AppSumo, StackSocial, bundles, provider promo channels, lifetime flash sales). True $/TB/month price floor with free egress, stated at the 5 TB and 20 TB tiers, plus which providers run an annual promo window.
